To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in children with end-stage kidney disease during hemodialysis with a low calcium concentration (1.25 mmol/L) PTH levels increase, 2) the degree of PTH increase is dependent on the initial PTH level and the response to low serum calcium level during dialysis, 3) the response to low calcium level in children is different from that in healthy children, 4) the response is dependent on the degree of parathyroid gland dysfunction, 5
in children with end-stage of chronic renal failure the PTH level increases by 1.5 times during hypocalcemia induced by low serum calcium during hemodialysis.
in children with ESRD the PTH level increases during hypocalcemia, but this increase is lower than in healthy children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of low calcium dialysate during hemodialysis in children with ESRD.
the possibility of using a low Ca dialysate in hemodialysis sessions to decrease PTH levels in patients with ESRD.
the influence of low calcium level in dialysate on PTH secretion in children with end-stage chronic renal failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the decrease in serum calcium during hemodialysis does not have a significant effect on the level of PTH in children with end-stage chronic renal disease.
in children with end-stage kidney disease a low calcium dialysate is a safe and effective method of treatment of secondary hyperparathyroidsm.
hypocalcemia during hemodialysis is a good method for the assessment of parathyroid gland reserve in patients with end-stage renal failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypocalcemic dialysis is an effective method for the control of secondary hyperparathyroid function in children with end-stage of renal disease.

in children with end-stage of chronic renal failure the PTH level is lower during hypocalcemia than in healthy subjects and in patients with hyperparathroidism the basal level of PTH is higher and the PTH response during hypocalcic stimulation is higher.
the PTH level in children with ESRD during hypocalcemia is not always elevated and the PTH level increase in response to hypocalcemia may be lower than in healthy subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of low calcium dialysate during dialysis session may be useful in children with ESRD.
the PTH level increases during hypocalcemia.
the use of hypocalcemic dialysate is an effective tool in the diagnosis of parathyroid gland disorders.
